question: A tent is cylindrical upto a height of 6 m and conical above it. The diameter of the base is 90 m and the height of the conical part is 28 m. What is the area (in m²) of canvas used in making it?
solution:
Given:

A tent is cylindrical up to a height of 6 m and conical above it.

The diameter of the base is 90 m and the height of the conical part is 28 m. 

Formula used:

Curved surface area = πrl

where r = radius of the base and l = slant height

Curved surface of a cylinder = 2πrh

where r = Radius of the base, h = height

Diameter = Radius × 2

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6300ef90c148e2f8399c4d453b1203b279dae082db7aa65ff1107278fd7ad819.png] 

The radius of the base = 90 ÷ 2 = 45m

Hence,

The radius of the base of the cylindrical part = 45m

The radius of the base of the conical part = 45m

Thus, the length of the slant height of the conical part = sqrt {45² + 28²} = 53m

Hence,

The curved surface area of the conical area

⇒ π × 45 × 53 = 2385π m²

The curved surface area of the cylindrical area

⇒ 2π × 45 × 6 = 540π m2

Now, the area of canvas used in making it = (2385 + 540)π = 2925π m²

**∴ The area of canvas used in making it is 2925π m2.**
